newsitem.title: FRANCE: Sanofi stock falls on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Sanofi stock falls on profit-taking.

text.p: Shares in pharmaceuticals group Sanofi retreated 2.6 percent on Tuesday after the company confirmed it had issued a warning about one of its medications, triggering profit-taking on the stock's sharp recent gains.
Sanofi, controlled by Elf Aquitaine, said it was removing its Trancopal muscle relaxant from the market and had notified doctors it caused side-effects.
Traders said the recall of the medicine, whose sales represent 300 million francs out of a group total of 23 billion, served as a pretext for profit-taking.
The share, which has risen more than 40 percent since the beginning of the year and hit a historic high of 473 francs on Friday, were down 2.71 percent at 448.50 francs at 1435 GMT.
The CAC-40 index was down 1.2 percent at the same time.
